scope: Sources and fixtures come from the OpenMS4-cli, OpenMS4-topp and OpenMS4-test-data packages, which are versioned independently of the Core SDK. They are deliberately not resolved against the Core SDK checkout.
method: MzMLSplitter transcribed from the pinned C++ topp package. The retained C++ outputs are compared canonically -- record counts, native identifiers, MS levels, retention times and peak values -- not byte for byte, because the upstream test itself uses FuzzyDiff and the two mzML writers differ in serialisation detail.
evidence_tier: executed differential (tier 1), canonical comparison against retained C++ tool output

real_data_differential.purpose: The port refused this input with exit 3, 'Unable to read file (parse error on line 0: precursor spectrum reference does not name an output spectrum)', after writing part 1 of 4. The mzML writer required every precursor spectrumRef to name a spectrum of the part being written; source MzMLHandler::writePrecursor_ resolves nothing.
real_data_differential.result: Both implementations write four parts with the same record split (10937/10936/10936/10936). Decoded comparison with the benchmark harness's equiv.py: 43,745 spectrum pairs and 1 chromatogram pair, 87,492 binary arrays compared, 87,492 bitwise equal, no peak-count mismatch. Part 2 carries 10,101 precursor references of which 4 are to scan=10929 (held by part 1) on both sides. Remaining metadata differences are the pre-existing identifier-spelling and processing-provenance class recorded by the 2026-09-15 benchmark, not this tool's data.
real_data_differential.wall_and_peak_rss: port 19.50 s / 4,370,788 KiB at 1 thread and 19.97 s / 4,370,648 KiB at 32 threads; C++ 12.95 s / 1,563,648 KiB at 1 thread. The node was shared, so treat the times as indicative.
real_data_differential.thread_invariance: All four parts are byte-identical between 1 and 32 threads.
